question:
A male child aged two and a half years is evaluated for a 3-4 day history of fever and worsening cough.
His symptoms began two weeks ago with mild cough and rhinorrhea. The patient appears fatigued with
decreased activity and appetite. His medical history is unremarkable with no prior hospitalizations,
though he has not received routine vaccinations due to parental choice. His growth and development
have been normal. There is no illness among household contacts, and he does not attend daycare.
Physical examination reveals an ill-appearing child with respiratory rate 35/min, heart rate 130/min,
temperature 38.9°C, and oxygen saturation 94%. Lung examination indicates right lower lobe
consolidation. Chest X-ray confirms right lower lobe pneumonia and reveals a posterior mediastinal
mass. Biopsy of the mass demonstrates rosettes with central fibrillar material and mature ganglion
cells. Which of the following statements is most accurate? Answer Choices: (A) This tumor has a low
likelihood of metastasizing to the bone (B) This tumor is associated with elevated catecholamine
metabolites in the urine (C) This tumor originates from the epithelial cells in the mediastinum (D) This

child might develop periorbital ecchymoses (E) This tumor’s origin is primarily mesenchymal in nature
(F) This tumor is generally localized and does not have a high risk of spreading in distance (G) The
biopsy findings are consistent with a thymoma (H) Most of the times the tumors of this kind are thoracic
in location (I) This tumor is most commonly associated with respiratory symptoms only (J) The tumor is
likely to arise from lymphoid tissue in the mediastinum
 A. The biopsy findings are consistent with a thymoma
B. This tumor is associated with elevated catecholamine metabolites in the urine
C. The tumor is likely to arise from lymphoid tissue in the mediastinum
D. This child might develop periorbital ecchymoses
E. This tumor has a low likelihood of metastasizing to the bone
F. This tumor is most commonly associated with respiratory symptoms only
G. This tumor originates from the epithelial cells in the mediastinum
H. This tumor’s origin is primarily mesenchymal in nature
I. Most of the times the tumors of this kind are thoracic in location
J. This tumor is generally localized and does not have a high risk of spreading in distance
